value.content: {"id": "portswigger_graphql", "item_type": "methodology", "topic": "graphql", "category": "PortSwigger Web Security: GraphQL API Vulnerabilities", "name": "GraphQL API Introspection, Batching & Authorization Methodology", "cwe": "CWE-200", "owasp_category": "A01:2021 - Broken Access Control", "signals": ["graphql_endpoint_exposed", "schema_introspection_enabled", "batching_query_supported", "circular_relation_dos", "missing_field_level_authorization", "alias_overload"], "verification_strategy": "Send a standard introspection query ({__schema{types{name}}}) to map available queries, mutations, and hidden fields. Test query batching (sending multiple operations in a single request array) to test for rate-limit bypasses on authentication mutations. Test object-level authorization on exposed mutations.", "evidence_requirements": ["introspection_schema_dump", "batch_execution_response", "unauthorized_field_disclosure"], "tools": [{"tool": "clairvoyance", "cmd": "clairvoyance -o schema.json https://example.com/graphql", "desc": "Recovers GraphQL API schemas even when introspection is partially restricted"}, {"tool": "httpx", "cmd": "httpx -u url/graphql -probe -d '{\"query\":\"{__typename}\"}'", "desc": "Detects active GraphQL endpoints and schema reflection"}], "remediation": "Disable schema introspection in production environments. Enforce query depth and complexity limits to prevent resource exhaustion. Apply rigorous object-level access control checks within resolver functions.", "description": "PortSwigger GraphQL labs explore uncovering hidden GraphQL endpoints, dumping schema documentation via introspection, bypassing brute-force defenses using query batching, and exploiting CSRF over GraphQL."}
